highlights: Review proposed file changes in the app: browse them, read feedback, edit comments, and ask the agent about specific changed lines.
A redesigned sidebar keeps tasks organized, lets you reorder pinned tasks, and helps you find tasks and project files faster.
Attach general files and images more easily, preview images and videos, and save unfinished prompts with their attachments for later.
New plugins connect to UC San Diego Kuali Build and n8n, using your own sign-in or API key and only the permissions you authorize.
Opt-in computer use lets the app work on your desktop with visible setup and activity, and updates install more reliably.
You can now download and install app updates from inside the app, with progress, release notes, and an automatic restart.
Each model now uses the correct account key, and you can replace or remove keys without restarting the app.
Signing in to add-ons such as GitHub, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365 is easier and more flexible.
When the app asks you to approve work, you now see complete details, including full proposed file changes.
Many small fixes make the app more stable and polished, including a refreshed look and better voice input on Mac.
Memory now keeps daily notes of your work by default, and you can optionally sync them between your computers through OneDrive.
New chats now start with the Flash model, and GPT-6.1 Sol is among the updated cloud models.
Finished tasks are now marked Done, and you can reopen them if you want to continue.
On Windows, the app no longer opens an extra console window when it works with your desktop applications.

setup: To update the app, open Settings, then About, and choose Check for Updates.
faq: Computer use is off by default; turn it on in Settings under General if you want the agent to work with local applications.
New tasks start in Full access, where the agent works without asking. Pick a different mode before sending if you want approvals first.
privacy: Memory is on by default and keeps daily notes of your conversations on your own computer. You can turn it off under Settings, General, Memory.
Syncing notes to your other computers through OneDrive is optional. Turn it on under Settings, General, Memory, and sign in with your UC San Diego account.
skills: Find reusable skills for recurring work in TritonAI Commons, the public skill library under Settings, Skills.
citizen: Bring back a prompt you already sent by pressing the up arrow in an empty message box.
If you want the agent to pause for your approval before changing files, choose Supervised mode before sending your task.
models: Check which access key is in use under Settings, Runtime. It shows only the last four characters, so the full key stays hidden.
To replace an access key, choose Change key, enter the new one, and pick Check access and save. The connection briefly restarts afterward.

highlights: You can now sign in with your UCSD account. Signing in is optional, and once you do, the app renews your session automatically.
New tool connections for Lucid and Tableau are included, and the list of available tools is now sorted alphabetically so connections are easier to find.
Saved notes that sync through OneDrive are better protected: notes are kept when two computers are confused for each other, and turning sync off now cancels a pending OneDrive sign-in.
Starting a new chat now places your cursor in the message box right away, and status labels in project folders are back.

setup: To update the app, open Settings, choose About, and click Check for Updates. Use the full TritonAI Installer only for first-time setup or repairs.
Do not install the public t3 package or t3.codes scripts; they install a different distribution, not the UCSD-managed TritonAI Harness.
faq: Computer use, which lets the agent click and type in your local apps, is off by default. Turn it on under Settings, General, Computer use; on a Mac it will ask for Accessibility and Screen Recording access.
Each chat has its own permission setting for when the agent asks before acting. New chats start in Full access unless you choose another mode before sending.
privacy: Memory, which keeps daily summaries of your chats as notes on your computer, is on by default. You can turn it off under Settings, General, Memory; your existing notes stay.

Notes stay on each computer unless you separately turn on Sync memory with OneDrive, which copies them to your OneDrive and brings in notes from your other computers. The app also sends anonymous usage counts; it does not include your prompts, responses, or file contents.
skills: Find reusable skills from the campus community in Settings, Skills, under TritonAI Commons. Skills you create stay under Your Skills until you choose to share them.
citizen: If you want the agent to pause before changing files or running commands, pick Supervised for that chat. It is a good choice the first time you run an unfamiliar task.
Give the agent a task in your own words and attach the files it needs. If the agent is already working, your new message waits in line and sends when it finishes.
models: TritonAI Harness comes with a managed Codex engine connected to TritonAI. You need a TritonAI API key and an internet connection for setup; the installer configures access for you.
